A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and provide readable main text, equations, all 11 figures, and Appendices A and B. Reflow and expanded references do not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments, synthetic reasoning experiments, intrinsic-dimension analyses, and language-model evaluations on mathematics benchmarks, documented in Figures 1–9 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and their experimental documentation in Appendix A.

M1.justification: The CoT and extended-thinking procedures, experimental model architectures, training objectives, tokenization, and inference procedures are unchanged. The equation correction does not introduce a different method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same CIFAR-100 tasks, synthetic classification and logical-deduction tasks, GSM8k, WikiText-2, MATH-500, and AIME 2022–2024 coverage. No dataset or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The direct-prediction, CoT, extended-thinking, and GSM8k Direct comparisons retain the same participants. Newly cited works in v2 are not introduced as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix A retains the same training budgets, model configurations, sample sizes, test sets, decoding settings, prompts, and AIME grouping procedure. No evaluation protocol is added or substantively revised.

E4.justification: The reasoning-structure and tokenization analyses in Figure 5, degree/depth sweeps in Figures 7–8, and alternative dimensionality estimators in Appendix A.2 and Figure 9 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report 10 replicates for the structure experiments, 20 for the synthetic thinking experiments, and five answer generations for benchmark evaluations. Figure 8 retains the same standard-error reporting.

E6.justification: Corresponding result plots, numerical statements, and qualitative findings are unchanged, including the CIFAR-100 fit 0.036 m^0.31 + 0.02 and the reasoning-length trends. No result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: Equation (2) gains missing brackets around the probability difference, correctly making q(x) multiply both terms. This repairs the displayed identity used in the Lipschitz bound; the assumptions, scaling argument, and optimal degree/depth derivations otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same claims about classification-error scaling, balanced reasoning trees, an optimal degree, and limits to improvements from extending reasoning depth.

C2.justification: Remark 6 previously attributed the gap between learned and task intrinsic dimensionality to limited data. v2 also identifies model architecture as a cause, modestly broadening the mechanism explanation while retaining the same prediction about optimal reasoning length.

D1.justification: Appendix A preserves the architecture, optimizer, learning-rate, tokenizer, data-generation, decoding, and complete prompting details. No technical disclosure or code/data access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 5 newly cites Wang et al., Beyond the 80/20 rule, for efficient reasoning. Appendix B replaces the robotics citation to Ahn et al. with Antonova et al. Most other reference changes update publication metadata for existing works; the central research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds acknowledgements, a generic impact statement, and conference publication information, alongside localized wording corrections and bibliographic updates. The main narrative and section/appendix organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: All 11 figures retain their graphical content. Caption wrapping, figure placement, bibliography layout, and appendix text boxes reflow; the final FAQ now ends on a mostly empty page. These are limited layout changes rather than new visual evidence.

improvement.justification: Correcting the probability weighting in Equation (2) removes a mathematical expression error, while Remark 6 more accurately acknowledges architectural limitations. These limited gains in precision leave the main conclusions and empirical support unchanged; less compact appendix pagination is a small drawback.
